name: Faster Rebuild Plan
description: Speed up background project mart large rebuilds with better observability, machine-aware worker memory defaults, burst execution, and safer DuckDB isolation so refresh ack and retained-row drain can catch up on both laptops and larger machines.

userStories.title: Expose effective worker runtime diagnostics
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want the worker to expose its effective DuckDB runtime settings and process memory signals so rebuild tuning can use live data instead of shell-only inspection.
acceptanceCriteria: Add an admin/debug path or extend an existing admin path to report the effective worker `DUCKDB_MEMORY_LIMIT`, temp directory, and relevant runtime config used by the background writer.
Include worker-side process memory data that is cheap to collect, such as RSS, so rebuild tuning can compare configured memory with actual worker usage.
The diagnostics are available from the running writer without requiring manual `ps` or environment inspection.
`bun test src/server/utils/backgroundServerStack.test.ts` passes
`bun test src/server/utils/projectMartLargeRebuildHeartbeat.test.ts` passes
`bun test src/server/services/projectMartLargeRebuildRunner.test.ts` passes
`bun run lint` passes

Live verify after implementation: worker reports the effective DuckDB memory limit, large rebuild cursor advances multiple batches per wake, `lastAckSeq` starts moving, `retainedRowCount` declines, temp dir does not grow explosively, and API latency remains acceptable while rebuild is active

userStories.title: Add rebuild and DuckDB queue observability
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want rebuild cycle timing and DuckDB queue metrics so we can tell when throughput is limited by polling, queue wait, or query execution.
acceptanceCriteria: Record large rebuild cycle metrics including phase, rows processed, and cycle duration in a way that can be inspected from an admin/debug path.
Expose main and background DuckDB queue depth or wait-time metrics so rebuild contention can be distinguished from memory pressure and idle polling.
The metrics are lightweight enough to leave enabled in ordinary local development.

userStories.title: Make background worker DuckDB memory default machine-aware
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want the split background writer to choose a safer default DuckDB memory cap based on host RAM so large rebuilds are not artificially constrained on bigger machines while smaller laptops stay protected.
acceptanceCriteria: Replace the fixed `4GB` fallback in `src/server/utils/backgroundServerStack.ts` with a machine-aware default derived from total host memory.
Keep `BACKGROUND_WRITER_DUCKDB_MEMORY_LIMIT` and `DUCKDB_MEMORY_LIMIT` as explicit overrides that win over the automatic default.
Add tests that cover at least low-memory, mid-memory, and higher-memory machine tiers for the worker DuckDB limit selection.

`bun test src/server/utils/projectMartLargeRebuildHeartbeat.test.ts` passes
`bun test src/server/services/projectMartLargeRebuildRunner.test.ts` passes
`bun run lint` passes

userStories.title: Raise portable rebuild throughput defaults
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want the default large rebuild batch size and idle poll interval to reflect practical catch-up behavior so rebuilds stop sleeping through obvious work.
acceptanceCriteria: Increase the default `PROJECT_MART_LARGE_REBUILD_BATCH_SIZE` to a portable non-trivial value instead of `1`.
Lower the default `PROJECT_MART_LARGE_REBUILD_POLL_INTERVAL_MS` from `5000` to a faster idle poll suitable for ordinary development machines.
Update tests and env-loading expectations to match the new defaults without requiring env overrides.

userStories.title: Run bounded rebuild bursts per wake
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want each heartbeat wake to process multiple rebuild cycles when useful so the worker can keep advancing without waiting for the next timer tick after every batch.
acceptanceCriteria: Add a bounded `PROJECT_MART_LARGE_REBUILD_MAX_CYCLES_PER_WAKE` control with a sensible default for portable machines.
The heartbeat runs consecutive cycles within one wake until it hits completion, idle, failure, pause, no-progress protection, or the configured per-wake limit.
Tests cover at least the single-wake burst path and one early-stop condition.

userStories.title: Move large rebuild executor work off the main DuckDB queue
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want large rebuild batch queries and statements to stop contending with the main control-plane DuckDB queue so higher rebuild throughput does not starve shorter writer operations.
acceptanceCriteria: Route large rebuild executor reads and writes onto the background DuckDB queue or another dedicated rebuild execution path instead of the normal serialized control queue.
Keep rebuild execution serialized initially so functional behavior does not change while queue isolation is introduced.
Rebuild metrics make it possible to see the effect of the queue move on cycle timing and queue pressure.

userStories.title: Add a documented catch-up tuning profile
userStories.description: As a maintainer, I want repo-native guidance for portable defaults and larger-machine catch-up overrides so rebuild tuning is repeatable across laptops and stronger hosts.
acceptanceCriteria: Document the recommended portable defaults for rebuild batch size, idle poll interval, per-wake cycle burst, and background worker DuckDB memory limit selection.
Document a stronger catch-up profile for larger-memory machines and a conservative profile for smaller machines.
Document which live signals to watch when tuning, including memory usage, temp growth, queue metrics, `lastAckSeq`, and retained row drain.
